title: TAPS grid for the three poems
subject: English
unit: Summer 1: Poetry: voice, hope and identity
source: Written for english/y8 lesson 60 (TAPS grid for the three poems (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 60: The power of poetry: TAPS and comparing ideas. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

model.title: Compare how two poets present the importance of stories.

parts.text: Theme: both explore stories that might be lost
Attitude: Agard angry then proud; Alareer calm and hopeful
Poetic methods: dialect and repetition / symbol and plea
Structure: drilled lists to a breakaway voice / a condition to a hope

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Both Agard and Alareer present stories as precious and fragile. Agard, at first angry and finally proud, uses dialect and repetition to reclaim a hidden history, whereas Alareer calmly uses the symbol of a kite and a plea to ask that his own story survive.

keywords.def: a big idea a text explores
the poet's feelings or viewpoint about the theme
a big idea that connects two texts
theme, attitude, poetic methods, structure: a frame for comparing poems

questions.q: Model with me: complete the TAPS row for 'Attitude' for Blessing and Agard
questions.a: Blessing: joyful but aware of injustice; Agard: angry, then proud.

questions.q: Write one sentence linking two poems with 'both'
questions.a: For example: 'Both Dharker and Alareer find hope in hardship.'

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a TAPS introduction comparing two of the poems on hope or identity. Starter: 'Both [poet] and [poet] present...'
questions.a: A TAPS introduction naming both poems, theme, attitudes, methods and structure, with a conceptual link.

questions.q: Extend: write a second conceptual link for a different pair
questions.a: A precise link, e.g. Agard and Dharker on communities overlooked by the powerful.

questions.q: Stretch: which pairing gives the richest comparison? Justify
questions.a: A reasoned choice with a shared idea and a clear difference.

questions.q: Which is the strongest conceptual link for Agard and Alareer?
options: both insist that stories must be told and carried
questions.a: C) both insist that stories must be told and carried. Agard claims a hidden history; Alareer asks for his story to be carried.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: what do the three poems have in common?
questions.a: For example: each gives a voice to people who might not be heard.
